html:
The Pame and the Chichimeca Jonaz are two related peoples of the dry uplands of north-central Mexico, in San Luis Potosí, Querétaro and Guanajuato. Both speak Oto-Pamean languages, related to Otomi.

They were among the peoples the Spanish and Aztecs called Chichimecas, the "barbarians" of the north. After silver was found at Zacatecas in 1546, the road to the mines crossed their lands, and the Chichimeca War (about 1550 to 1590) followed. Spain ended it with gifts of food and cloth, missions and settlements of Tlaxcalan colonists, rather than by conquest. In the 1700s Franciscans built missions among the Pame in the Sierra Gorda of Querétaro.

The Chichimeca Jonaz today live mainly at Misión de Chichimecas near San Luis de la Paz in Guanajuato, in Mexico.
